lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The bakery role appears before the quantitative research internship and research assistant role.
items.because: That ordering makes the current store-management job define the page’s direction before the relevant research experience.

items.says: The dates show a shift into bakery management immediately after the quantitative research internship without explaining the change in direction.
The opening-shift description does not show what you did to keep labour costs within budget.
items.because: It gives the team size and budget outcome but not the staffing decision connecting them.

items.says: The 35% improvement does not identify the risk-adjusted metric or its comparison strategy.
items.because: A quant reader cannot tell what rose by 35% or what the smoother improved upon.

items.says: The description does not show how costs affected the position smoother.
Purged splits and an embargo do not establish that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They address leakage between training and test periods, not decision-time availability for every feature, transformation and simulated execution.

items.says: The explanatory clause makes the validation line longer without adding a necessary result.
items.because: Cutting it would leave room for the more consequential finding of the validation.

items.says: The six-year validation description does not state what the test found.
items.because: The data span shows the scale of the exercise, not its outcome.

items.says: The reuse result is buried after the description of the feature store.
The live-allocation approval is buried after the presentation details.
items.because: Leading with the approval would make the consequence clear before listing what was presented.

items.says: The best backtested Sharpe among 400 configurations is not an expected live Sharpe without further validation.
items.because: Selecting the highest result introduces selection bias, so it is an observed backtest Sharpe rather than a defensible live-performance expectation.

items.says: The reported Sharpe has no stated value.
items.because: The number of configurations does not show how the selected one performed.

items.says: The line does not say whether the selected result changed a decision.
The desk book’s Sharpe improvement is buried after the signal description.
items.because: The change from 1.1 to 1.5 is the line’s clearest measured result.

items.says: The strongest Northpeak bullet is not the first bullet in the entry.
items.because: The opening bullet lacks a named metric and comparator, while this one gives a before-and-after Sharpe ratio and its test context.

items.says: “Running the runs” repeats the same word awkwardly.
The variance-bound result is not the opening bullet of the research assistant entry.
“My proof tightens” uses a personal pronoun and present tense for work in a past role.
The download count shows reach but not what users gained from the package.
The finding on 24 indices is buried after the description of the significance tests.
items.because: Starting with the tests delays the result and makes the line harder to scan.

items.says: The two crisis periods used for the robustness claim are not identified.
“Them” makes the reader look back to identify what the 24 refers to.
The passive wording leaves it unclear whether you presented the paper yourself.
“Wrote up” is a conversational opening for the working-paper contribution.
The modeling description does not say what the models achieved.
items.because: Training models establishes the activity but not whether it improved performance or produced a competitive result.

items.says: The feature work is too broad to show what you contributed technically.
The bullet repeats the competition context already stated in the entry heading.
The 0.02 validation-to-leaderboard gap does not name its scoring metric.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the units or importance of the gap without knowing what was scored.

items.says: The validation-leakage result is not the opening bullet of the competition entry.
The 2023 competition bullet wrongly attributes the futures-book order-book signal result also credited to the 2025 Northpeak internship.
items.because: The internship reports the same 0.4 Sharpe-ratio increase over an 18-month out-of-sample backtest, making the achievement and its provenance doubtful.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: The misspelling can distract from the skill and make the section look unchecked.

items.says: The Kafka listing has no supporting messaging or streaming work in the experience entries.
